attempts.label: CRCNS:bf-1
attempts.entry_title: Basal forebrain gamma in home cage and arena (Nair et al. 2018)
attempts.summary: The main finding, that basal forebrain gamma is lower in the arena than in the home cage, held in direction and significance, but the drop was 48% against the paper's 35%. Gamma rising with movement in the home cage did not reproduce under the fixed test, which cannot detect a within-rat effect in so few rats, though gamma rose in every rat. Gamma rising with time in the arena held in sign but not in size, and the brief excursions to the home-cage state did not match in count or duration. The cortical, single-unit, behavior and object findings could not be tested because the data set holds only basal forebrain LFP.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Nair, Klaassen, Arato, Vyssotski, Harvey and Rainer (2018) on CRCNS data set bf-1, which holds basal forebrain LFP from six rats in two home-cage and two arena sessions each, with a movement-sensor value per 2-s segment. It measures the reduction of BF gamma power in the arena, its relation to movement and to time in the arena, the low-frequency bands, the unimodality of theta and gamma power, and excursions of gamma during exploration. The ACC, VC, single-unit, object and behaviour data of the paper are not in the data set.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Nair et al. (2018) from CRCNS bf-1

outcomes.statement: BF gamma power was reduced by 35 +/- 3% when rats moved from the home cage to the novel arena, a highly significant reduction.
outcomes.source: Results, BF Gamma Deactivation During Exploration, paragraph 1; Figure 3A
outcomes.quote: The main finding of the present study is a striking (35 ± 3%) and highly significant (paired t test, P < 10−5) reduction of this BF gamma activity when rats were transferred from their home cage to a novel, empty arena which they explored during a 10-min interval (Fig. 3A).
outcomes.notes: Home-cage gamma (mean periodogram power, 30-80 Hz) exceeds arena gamma in 6 of 6 rats; the reduction is 48.0% under reading (a) and 48.0% under reading (b), paired t test t = 3.84, p = 0.012 over 6 rats (11 session pairs, 47.7%, p = 0.00047). Every epoch (2 s, 10 s), artifact and pairing reading gives 46.8% to 48.1%, outside 35 +/- 3%, with p from 0.0002 to 0.014. Per rat the reduction is 37.3% to 63.9%. Leaving out 49-51 Hz (a line at 50 Hz in one file) gives 44.7%; the amplitude spectrum, which the data descriptor's example uses and the paper does not, gives 24.0%. The paper's p < 1e-5 rests on 22 hemispheres and is not reached with six rats (reported, not required by the criterion).
deviations: The data set gives one BF signal per rat for six rats, so tests run over rats (n = 6), or session pairs as a variant, where the paper used 22 hemispheres (claims file header). The two sessions of a condition are averaged per rat (n = 6); rat 3's home-cage session 2 is left out as a second deposit of its session 1, so rat 3's home cage is session 1 alone.

The segments come already down-sampled to 400 Hz and cleaned by the depositors. The SI's peak-to-peak rule applied again (claims file header, reading b) drops 16.8% of segments, against the SI's 1-4%; both readings are run.
The paper does not say how the spectrum is scaled or windowed; a plain periodogram is used (claims file header, a standard choice that cannot change a ratio).

outcomes.statement: The BF gamma reduction in the arena was significant in every one of the 22 hemispheres analyzed individually.
outcomes.source: Results, BF Gamma Deactivation During Exploration, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: BF gamma reductions were significant in all brain hemispheres (n = 22) when analyzed individually (unpaired t test P < 0.01).

statistics.n: 22 hemispheres, each tested on its own

outcomes.notes: All 12 arena recordings have lower gamma than the home-cage recording of the same session number, unpaired t test over epochs, largest p = 2.7e-30 (2-s), 1.9e-20 (peak-to-peak rule), 1.1e-07 (10-s). Rat 3's arena session 2 is tested against both of rat 3's home-cage files, p < 1e-100 either way with 2-s epochs as delivered, 7.1e-80 and 4.7e-93 under the peak-to-peak rule, 6.2e-30 and 6.8e-33 with 10-s epochs.
deviations: The unit is a rat and session (12 recordings) where the paper tested 22 hemispheres (criterion).

outcomes.statement: In the arena, BF gamma power did not vary with movement-sensor quartile.
outcomes.source: Results, BF Gamma Deactivation During Exploration, paragraph 2; Figure 3B
outcomes.quote: This analysis, shown in Fig. 3B, demonstrates that BF gamma activity in the arena was largely unrelated to locomotor behavior (one-way ANOVA...
outcomes.notes: Per-rat quartile means of arena gamma 32.3, 32.7, 32.0, 33.5 (quartiles within each recording), one-way ANOVA F = 0.005, p = 1.0, eta squared 0.0007; quartiles within each rat p = 0.998. Variants give p > 0.1 too (ANOVA over epochs p = 0.60 and 0.19; repeated-measures p = 0.38 and 0.28; 10-s epochs and the peak-to-peak rule p >= 0.99; movement shifted by one segment p >= 0.998). The one-way ANOVA on quartile means divided by each rat's mean, a variant, gives p = 0.12 and 0.33. The criterion's test cannot see a within-rat effect against the between-rat spread (it misses the home-cage rise), so the variants are the informative ones; all give p > 0.1.
deviations: The data set gives one BF signal per rat for six rats, so tests run over rats (n = 6), or session pairs as a variant, where the paper used 22 hemispheres (claims file header). outcomes.statement: In the home cage, BF gamma power increased with movement-sensor quartile.
outcomes.source: Results, BF Gamma Deactivation During Exploration, paragraph 2; Figure 3B
outcomes.quote: BF gamma activity increased with locomotor behavior in the home cage (one-way ANOVA...
outcomes.notes: Home-cage gamma rises from the first to the fourth movement quartile in 6 of 6 rats (means 50.3, 62.1, 68.4, 72.0; Q4/Q1 1.43), but the criterion's one-way ANOVA over quartiles on per-rat quartile means gives F = 0.31, p = 0.82 (quartiles within each rat p = 0.77, eta squared 0.045), because per-rat home-cage gamma ranges from 36 to 145. Variants that take the rat into account find the rise (repeated-measures ANOVA p = 2.0e-05; ANOVA over epochs p = 3.9e-46; one-way ANOVA on quartile means divided by each rat's mean p = 1.6e-09), and no epoch, artifact or movement-shift reading brings the one-way p below 0.74. Whether the per-rat one-way ANOVA is the paper's test is asked of a reader (questions/crcns-bf-1.yaml), and what the paper's observations were is asked of its authors (findings).
deviations: The data set gives one BF signal per rat for six rats, so tests run over rats (n = 6), or session pairs as a variant, where the paper used 22 hemispheres (claims file header). The two sessions of a condition are averaged per rat (n = 6); rat 3's home-cage session 2 is left out as a second deposit of its session 1, so rat 3's home cage is session 1 alone.

The segments come already down-sampled to 400 Hz and cleaned by the depositors. The SI's peak-to-peak rule applied again (claims file header, reading b) drops 16.8% of segments, against the SI's 1-4%; both readings are run.
The paper does not say what the ANOVA's observations are; the criterion takes per-rat quartile means, and the epoch-level and repeated-measures tests are shown as variants.

outcomes.statement: Gamma suppression in the arena remained highly significant when epochs matched for movement were compared, for example the fourth home-cage quartile against the third arena quartile.
outcomes.source: Results, BF Gamma Deactivation During Exploration, paragraph 2; Figure 3B
outcomes.quote: gamma suppression during exploration remained highly significant when LFP epochs matched for movement were analyzed (e.g., the fourth and third movement quartiles for home cage and arena, respectively; one-way ANOVA
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), home-cage Q4 against arena Q3, and reading (b), the closest mean movement values, pick the same pair (mean movement 356 against 333). Home-cage gamma 72.0 against arena 32.0, higher in 6 of 6 rats, but the one-way ANOVA of the per-rat means gives p = 0.070 (quartiles within each rat p = 0.070). A paired t test of the same values, a variant, gives p = 0.0071; matching quartiles within each rat gives one-way p = 0.099 and paired p = 0.0091. The one-way ANOVA on the two values divided by each rat's mean, a variant, gives p = 7.5e-08. The choice of test is asked of a reader with fig3b-home-cage-gamma-increases-with-movement (questions/crcns-bf-1.yaml).

outcomes.statement: BF gamma was larger in the home cage than in either of the two daily arena sessions, and slightly larger (5.62 +/- 1.2%) in the second arena session than in the first, with no interaction between day and session.
outcomes.source: Results, BF Gamma Deactivation During Exploration, paragraph 2; Figure 3C
outcomes.quote: was larger in the home cage than during either of the two arenaexploration sessions (two-way ANOVA with factors day and session and post hoc tests... In addition, gamma activity was slightly increased during the second arena-exploration session compared with the first session (5.62 ± 1.2%; post hoc test... and there was no significant interaction between day and session number.

statistics.about: home cage against each arena session
statistics.test: two-way ANOVA with factors day and session, post hoc tests

outcomes.notes: Per-rat gamma, home cage 62.7, arena session 1 35.4 and arena session 2 29.8 (means over rats). The home cage exceeds both arena sessions by Bonferroni-corrected paired t tests (p = 0.038 and 0.035; peak-to-peak rule 0.045 and 0.041; 10-s epochs 0.038 and 0.033) but not by Tukey's HSD on per-rat values (p = 0.30 and 0.19), which treats the 18 values as independent groups and ignores the pairing within rat. The criterion names Tukey as the standard reading and the paired tests as a variant; the outcome rests on the variant, chosen because the rats are paired across conditions. The second part, a rise from the first to the second daily arena session, cannot be tested: the descriptor calls sessions 1 and 2 two separate examples of each session type, and nothing in the data set gives a day or the order of trials. Arena session 2 is 15.9% below session 1 (group means -15.7%, paired t p = 0.020), against +5.62 +/- 1.2%; this is reported and not judged.
deviations: The data set gives one BF signal per rat for six rats, so tests run over rats (n = 6), or session pairs as a variant, where the paper used 22 hemispheres (claims file header). The two sessions of a condition are averaged per rat (n = 6); rat 3's home-cage session 2 is left out as a second deposit of its session 1, so rat 3's home cage is session 1 alone.

The segments come already down-sampled to 400 Hz and cleaned by the depositors. The SI's peak-to-peak rule applied again (claims file header, reading b) drops 16.8% of segments, against the SI's 1-4%; both readings are run.
The data set has no day labels, so the day factor is dropped and the arena sessions are compared within rat by a paired t test, as the criterion says.

The data set's session numbers are not taken as the first and second daily arena sessions. The descriptor calls them two separate examples (Session 1 and 2) of each session type, and rat 3's home-cage session 2 is an excerpt of its session 1, so the files may be chosen excerpts. The arena 2 against arena 1 part of the criterion is therefore not judged (metadata_insufficient), and the outcome rests on the home-cage part.

outcomes.statement: Within arena sessions BF gamma stayed suppressed but rose with time spent in the arena (r = 0.72, n = 22).
outcomes.source: Results, BF Gamma Deactivation During Exploration, paragraph 2; Figure 3D
outcomes.quote: While gamma activity was continuously suppressed in the arena, it was positively correlated with time spent in the arena (r = 0.72, n = 22, P < 10−4) during individual exploration sessions, as shown in Fig. 3D.
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), 1-min bins over the first 10 min, gamma averaged over the 12 arena recordings, r = 0.859, p = 0.0015 (n = 10 bins); its 2-s variant r = 0.197, p = 0.0006. Reading (b), mean of per-recording r, 0.129 (one-sample t p = 0.056; per recording -0.27 to 0.40). Reading (c), all epochs pooled, r = 0.045, p = 0.0094. No reading the criterion names puts r within 0.72 +/- 0.072; the correlation is positive at p < 0.05 under (a) and (c). With the 10-min window anchored at the file end (the transfer, on Fig. 3D's axis) (a) gives r = 0.885, p = 0.00066 and (b) r = 0.130, p = 0.021. Reading (b) does not depend on where a file's clock starts; over whole files it gives r = 0.165, p = 0.011. In 9 of 12 arena files the first minute has more movement than the middle, consistent with entry near t = 0 but not proof of it; several of the differences are small (403.9 against 389.2). Bin width moves r across the tolerance. Within tolerance are 30-s bins, 0.744 and 0.747 (start and end anchor), and 20-s bins with the end anchor, 0.662 (p = 6.9e-5); outside are 20-s bins from the start, 0.645, and 2-min bins, 0.860 and 0.969. The criterion names no partial outcome; partially reproduced is used because the positive correlation holds while its size at the criterion's 1-min bins does not match.
deviations: The data set gives one BF signal per rat for six rats, so tests run over rats (n = 6), or session pairs as a variant, where the paper used 22 hemispheres (claims file header). The two sessions of a condition are averaged per rat (n = 6); rat 3's home-cage session 2 is left out as a second deposit of its session 1, so rat 3's home cage is session 1 alone.
The paper's n = 22 matches its hemispheres; here 12 arena recordings.

Each file's clock starts at 0 and files run 8.8 to 13 min, longer than the SI's 10-min trial, and nothing says where arena entry is. The 10-min window is taken from the file start and, as a reading, from the file end; both give the same outcome, and reading (b) is shown over whole files, which needs no anchor.

Assumed 1-min bins for reading (a), as the criterion names them (Figure 3D's axis runs in minutes); the criterion says the bin width is open, and 30-s bins put r within tolerance (0.744 and 0.747), as do 20-s bins with the end anchor (0.662), which would give reproduced. Asked of the paper's authors with the question on what was correlated (findings).

outcomes.statement: In the BF, delta and beta power, like gamma, were higher in the home cage than in the arena, while theta power was strongly suppressed in the home cage.
outcomes.source: SI, Low-Frequency Power Modulations in Home Cage and Arena, paragraph 2; Fig. S2
outcomes.quote: In the BF, in addition to the gamma enhancement in the home cage, beta and delta oscillations are also elevated, whereas theta power is strongly suppressed relative to values recorded in the arena.
outcomes.notes: Over 6 rats, home cage against arena, delta 334 against 223 (p = 0.030), theta 161 against 252 (p = 0.00045), beta 46.7 against 35.0 (p = 0.024), gamma 62.7 against 32.6 (p = 0.012), paired t tests. All four bands hold in the stated directions under all 12 epoch, artifact and pairing readings.
deviations: The data set gives one BF signal per rat for six rats, so tests run over rats (n = 6), or session pairs as a variant, where the paper used 22 hemispheres (claims file header). The two sessions of a condition are averaged per rat (n = 6); rat 3's home-cage session 2 is left out as a second deposit of its session 1, so rat 3's home cage is session 1 alone.

The segments come already down-sampled to 400 Hz and cleaned by the depositors. The SI's peak-to-peak rule applied again (claims file header, reading b) drops 16.8% of segments, against the SI's 1-4%; both readings are run.

outcomes.statement: Within each condition, the distributions of BF theta and gamma power over 2-s epochs were unimodal, with no evidence of substates, in each of six rats.
outcomes.source: SI, Distributions of Theta and Gamma Power Within Each State Are Unimodal, paragraph 1; Fig. S3
outcomes.quote: These results were confirmed (at P > 0.1) in a total of six animals, in total yielding no evidence for multimodality in either behavioral state or frequency band.
outcomes.notes: Hartigan dip tests of 2-s theta and gamma power, per rat and condition, sessions pooled, 24 tests, smallest p = 0.554; each session alone, 46 tests (rat 3 has one home-cage file), smallest p = 0.102 (rat 5 home cage session 1, gamma); dip statistics 0.0065 to 0.028. The left-out duplicate file gives p = 0.99 and 0.96. On log10 power, a variant the criterion does not name (it tests power), the pooled reading gives p > 0.1 (smallest 0.462) and each session alone gives one test below 0.05, rat 5's home-cage session 1, gamma, p = 0.035, the test that gives the smallest p (0.102) on raw power.
deviations: The data set gives one BF signal per rat for six rats, so tests run over rats (n = 6), or session pairs as a variant, where the paper used 22 hemispheres (claims file header). The two sessions of a condition are averaged per rat (n = 6); rat 3's home-cage session 2 is left out as a second deposit of its session 1, so rat 3's home cage is session 1 alone.
P-values come from the diptest package's tabulated null distribution; the paper does not say how its p-values were obtained (a standard choice).

outcomes.statement: During about 20 min of arena exploration, BF gamma made on average eight brief excursions into the home-cage range, lasting 8 to 44 s (16 +/- 8 s), with a clear rise in gamma power (0.56 +/- 0.27) and no change in theta power (-0.01 +/- 0.82) relative to 4 to 8 s before the peak.
outcomes.source: SI, Analysis of Excursions to DMN Brain State During Arena Exploration, paragraph 2; Fig. S5
outcomes.quote: We found on average eight excursions during the 20 min spent in the arena, corresponding to about one excursion every 2–3 min. Excursions lasted between 8 and 44 s, with an average duration of 16 ± 8 s. Based on a comparison of LFP power at the gamma peak to the average values 4–8 s before the peak, gamma transitions were associated with clear increases in gamma power (0.56 ± 0.27, paired t tests... but no concomitant significant modulations in theta power (−0.01 ± 0.82, paired t tests... P > 0.1) were found.

statistics.about: gamma power at the peak against 4 to 8 s before
theta power at the peak against 4 to 8 s before

outcomes.notes: Across the 12 readings (scale raw, log10 or normalized; threshold from 20 bins or kernel density; arena sessions together or each alone), the gamma rise at the peak is significant in all (p 0.0001 to 0.04, paired t over 6 rats) and the theta change is not significant (p > 0.1) in 10, among them every log10 reading (raw and normalized scales with 20 bins and sessions together give theta p = 0.028 and 0.040). No reading matches the count or durations; 10.7 to 14.5 excursions per 20 min against 8, mean duration 5.1 to 5.6 s against 16 +/- 8 (within tolerance only at its lower bound, not reached), and durations from 2 s against the paper's shortest of 8 s; under log10 with 20 bins 13 of 82 excursions last 8 s or more. No reading puts the threshold near 2.6 (raw 25 to 109, log10 1.38 to 2.03, normalized 0.54 to 1.11), so the 0.56 and -0.01 values are reported and not judged (log10 rise 0.144, theta change 0.035). As a scale-free comparison, shown and not judged, the gamma rise over the mean threshold is 0.39 to 0.44 on the raw and normalized scales, against 0.56 / 2.6 = 0.215 in the paper.
deviations: The data set gives one BF signal per rat for six rats, so tests run over rats (n = 6), or session pairs as a variant, where the paper used 22 hemispheres (claims file header). The two sessions of a condition are averaged per rat (n = 6); rat 3's home-cage session 2 is left out as a second deposit of its session 1, so rat 3's home cage is session 1 alone.
The boxcar runs over the sequence of retained segments within a file; the two arena files are analysed as separate series, as they share no clock.
The paper's power scale, histogram bins and minimum excursion length are not given; the readings of the criterion are run and none gives durations of 8 s or more only.
At the ends of a file the boxcar averages the two values that exist (round 1 used zero padding, which lowered the end values to two thirds); the paper does not say how ends were handled.

outcomes.statement: In four more rats with bipolar BF electrodes, home-cage gamma was also strong and was reduced by 24 +/- 3% during arena exploration.
outcomes.source: Results, BF Gamma Deactivation During Exploration, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Strong BF gamma activity in the home cage was also observed in these bipolar recordings, and this oscillatory activity was again strongly suppressed during arena exploration, (24 ± 3% reduction; paired t tests... 10−4).
outcomes.notes: The paper's four bipolar rats are not identified in the data set. The descriptor and the files name rats 1 to 6 with one LFP channel each and say nothing about electrode type, so no recording can be taken as bipolar. The bucket holds no other files.

outcomes.statement: BF gamma power was consistent over the 3 days of testing.
outcomes.source: Results, BF Gamma Deactivation During Exploration, paragraph 2; Figure 3C
outcomes.quote: was consistent over the 3 d of testing (one-way ANOVA... (Fig. 3C)
outcomes.notes: The data set gives sessions 1 and 2 of each type with no day; the paper's arena exploration ran over 3 days. No file name, variable or document gives the day.

outcomes.statement: BF gamma increased rapidly when the rat was transferred back from the arena to its home cage.
outcomes.source: Results, BF Gamma Deactivation During Exploration, paragraph 2; Figure 3D
outcomes.quote: Nevertheless, gamma increased rapidly when the rat was transferred back to its home cage.
outcomes.notes: Needs a recording continuous across the transfer from arena to home cage. Each file has its own clock starting at 0 and holds one condition, so no recording spans a transfer, and no file can be placed in time relative to another.

outcomes.statement: In the arena, with or without objects, rats spent most of their time exploring the arena and the objects when present (87.8 +/- 3.6%), 7.6 +/- 1.7% grooming and 1.80 +/- 0.9% in quiet wakefulness (mean +/- SEM, seven rats, video tracking and motion sensor).
outcomes.source: Results, Behavioral Analyses, paragraph 1; Figure 2B
outcomes.quote: In the arena, tracking analyses showed that rats spent a large majority of their time (87.8 ± 3.6%, mean ± SEM) exploring the arena itself and objects when these were present. Only 7.6 ± 1.7% of the total time was spent grooming in this exploratory context, and animals were rarely in a state of quiet wakefulness (1.80 ± 0.9%).
outcomes.notes: Needs the video tracking and ELAN behaviour scoring of seven rats; the data set holds only LFP and one movement-sensor value per 2-s segment, and the paper names no other deposit.

outcomes.statement: Rats explored less in the home cage than in the arena with or without objects, and in the home cage they divided their time about equally between quiet wakefulness and grooming.

outcomes.statement: Of 49 well-isolated BF neurons in six rats, 25 were phase locked to broadband (30 to 80 Hz) gamma oscillations.
outcomes.source: Results, BF Gamma Deactivation During Exploration, paragraph 5; Figure 5A

findings.statement: Rat_3_Type_HCage_Session_2.mat is not a separate recording. 287 of its 291 segments are segments of Rat_3_Type_HCage_Session_1.mat with the same LFP and movement values, 100 s later on that file's clock (they cover 106 to 750 s of it). The data set presents it as a second home-cage session.

The data set holds only the BF LFP of six rats in home cage and arena. The ACC and VC recordings, single units, object sessions, video and behaviour scoring of the paper are not in it, and the paper names no other deposit; 16 of the 28 claims need data that are not in it.

The sessions carry no day and no time of recording, and each file has its own clock starting at 0, so the paper's day factor, the order of home-cage and arena sessions and the transfer between them cannot be reconstructed. Which electrodes were bipolar is not stated.

The LFP has no stated unit (its range is consistent with microvolts), and the movement value is dimensionless; its scale in rats 4 and 5 is about a quarter of that in the other rats, which is not explained.

Artifact segments were removed without a stated rule. Removed segments make up 2.6% to 23.5% of each file's span, more than the 1-4% the SI reports for its rule, and the SI's rule applied to the delivered segments removes a further 16.8%.
The descriptor names the home-cage condition 'Hcage' while the files use 'HCage', and describes basal_forebrain_lfp.tar.gz as a file of .mat files without saying it is a gzipped tar.

In 13 of 24 files the movement value of a segment correlates best with the 100-200 Hz LFP power of the next segment, and in 10 with the same segment, so the movement stream may lead the LFP by up to one 2-s segment. Rat 2's home-cage session 1 has a line at 50 Hz, 26 times its neighbours, inside the gamma band.

Question for the paper's authors. What were the observations of the one-way ANOVAs over movement quartiles (Fig. 3B), per-hemisphere quartile means or epochs, and was gamma normalized per animal? On this data set per-rat means give p = 0.82 for the home-cage rise and p = 0.07 for the movement-matched comparison, while repeated-measures and paired tests give p < 0.01.

Question for the paper's authors. How was the 35% reduction of gamma power computed (spectral estimate, scaling, averaging)? A periodogram mean over 30-80 Hz gives 48% on this data set, under every epoch, artifact and averaging reading.

The descriptor calls sessions 1 and 2 two separate examples of each session type and does not say whether they are the first and second arena trials of one day, the paper's two daily 10-min trials (Fig. 3C). Here session 2 has 15.9% lower gamma than session 1, where the paper reports 5.62% higher in the second trial, so the order matters and cannot be recovered.

Question for the paper's authors. For the excursions of Figs. S4 and S5, what was the power scale (the threshold of 2.6), how were histogram bins set, and was there a minimum excursion length? Without one, the readings tried give 10.7 to 14.5 excursions per 20 min lasting 5 s on average, against 8 lasting 8 to 44 s.

Question for the paper's authors. What was correlated with time in Fig. 3D (r = 0.72, n = 22), binned group means, per-session correlations or epochs, at what bin width, and from arena entry or back from the transfer? The readings give r = 0.86 (1-min bins), 0.74 (30-s bins), 0.13 (per recording) and 0.045 (pooled epochs).

verifications.reviewed: The handover of the first run, the executed notebook with the conclusions and summary removed, the helper module and the claims file. The verifier also read the paper and the data descriptor under paper/, listed the bucket's filelist.txt and S3 listing, and tested helper functions on synthetic inputs.

disagreements.reason: Home cage exceeds both arena files with Bonferroni-corrected paired t p = 0.038 / 0.035, but Tukey gives p = 0.30 / 0.19. Arena 2 is 15.9% below arena 1 (p = 0.02), but the data descriptor calls sessions 1 and 2 two separate examples, so nothing shows they are the first and second daily sessions; the session-order part should be blocked (metadata_insufficient). Rat 3's HCage session 2 being a 100-s-shifted excerpt of session 1 also suggests the files are chosen excerpts, so the reversed -15.9% is not evidence against the paper's +5.62% (problem 2). Tukey treats the 18 rat-level values as independent groups and ignores pairing within rat (problem 4, not affecting a conclusion).

verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook with the conclusions and the summary, the README, the attempt record and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier agrees with all 28 outcomes. Outside the claims, it found that the summary's count of data_missing claims read as 17, that the data_missing finding listed bipolar recordings, which are a metadata_insufficient matter, and that the README's run time had no printed support. The summary now says 15 claims besides fig3d-rapid-switch-to-home-cage, bipolar recordings are taken out of the data_missing finding, and the README no longer states a run time.

entries.name: crcns-bf-1-nair-2018
entries.title: Basal forebrain gamma in home cage and arena (Nair et al. 2018)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Nair, Klaassen, Arato, Vyssotski, Harvey and Rainer (2018) on CRCNS data set bf-1, which holds basal forebrain LFP from six rats in two home-cage and two arena sessions each, with a movement-sensor value per 2-s segment. It measures the reduction of BF gamma power in the arena, its relation to movement and to time in the arena, the low-frequency bands, the unimodality of theta and gamma power, and excursions of gamma during exploration. The ACC, VC, single-unit, object and behaviour data of the paper are not in the data set.
